sources.title: San Francisco sues Trump Media for selling early access to Trump posts
Early alerts: Trump Media plans paid fast-track access to Truth Social posts

claims.claim: San Francisco’s city attorney is urging a state court to block Trump’s social media platform Truth Social from offering customers who pay $100,000 per month priority access to the president’s and other high‑level officials’ posts before they’re available to other users.

claims.claim: The complaint says the $100,000‑per‑month Truth API lets customers view announcements that could move financial markets before they appear to other users, creating a financial advantage for the company and for President Trump, who owns 41 % of the company through a trust in which he is the sole beneficiary.
claims.bestSource: San Francisco Sues Trump’s Truth Social Over Paid Subscriptions - Bloomberg Law News
claims.evidence: San Francisco’s city attorney is urging a state court to block Trump’s social media platform Truth Social from offering customers who pay $100,000 per month priority access to the president’s and other high-level officials’ posts before they’re available to other users. The lawsuit comes on the heels of a similar one filed in federal court last week where two nonprofits challenged the constitutionality of the paid service called “Truth API.” Providing early access to subscribers of “announcements of consequential government decisions that can move financial markets” would create “a financial gain for Trump Media,” as well as for President Donald Trump , who owns 41% of Trump Media through a revocable trust in which he is the sole beneficiary, the lawsuit said. The key theory of the complaint is that Trump’s posts are tantamount to insider trading and unfair business practices. “Truth API disadvantages regular investors, including individuals who hold investments via pension funds, 401(k) plans, and other retirement funds, whose investment vehicles do not and/or cannot obtain Truth API’s early-access information,” the complaint said. On Monday a group of former prosecutors and federal agents filed an amicus brief in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York arguing the paid subscription could violate federal securities laws, the Trade Secrets Act, and could constitute illegal outside compensation for federal employment. The case is California v. Trump Media & Tech Grp. , Cal. Super. Ct., complaint filed 9/21/26. ( Updates with Trump Media comment in seventh paragraph. )
